Md. Mokhtar Hossain, Advocate ------ For the petitioners

parties:
Zainal Abedin
Vs.
Syed Hashmatullah and Others
full_judgment:
Amin-Ur-Rahman Khan J:—This Rule at the instance of the pre-emptee-petitioner is directed against the judgment and order of the Additional District-Judge, Rajshahi, in Misc. Appeal No. 32 of 1970 affirming the judgment and order of the Munsif, Nawabganj in Misc. Case N. 92 of 1968 allowing pre-emption in favour of the opposite party under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 2. The opposite party No. 1 being the petitioner brought Misc. Case No. 92 of 1968 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act seeking pre-emption of the land sold to the present petitioner upon the allegations that he was a co-sharer tenant by inheritance in the case holding and that the purchaser was a stranger and that no notice was served and the petitioner was not aware of the sale until 3.2.68. 

 8. Mr. Mokhtar Hossain stressed that according to subsection 2 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act all co-sharers by inheritance were required to be made parties while seeking pre-emption by another co-sharer tenant by inheritance and that this being a mandatory requirement of law the omission to make the parties made the pre-emption case liable to be dismissed. 

 10. In this case it was found by the learned Munsif that the brothers of Rezia or their heirs never claimed any interest in the case land nor took any steps to have their names recorded and also lived far away. He however was of the opinion that only the recorded co-sharer tenants and those who asserted their right in the tenancy should be made parties to enable them to claim pre-emption. The learned Additional District Judge concurred with the said findings. Thus from the findings of both the courts below it Could be seen that there were some co-sharer tenants by inheritance in the holding who were not made parties in the pre-emption case. But the courts below gave a wrong finding that even though they were co-sharer tenants by inheritance they were not necessary parties because they did not have their names recorded and did not claim interest in the case land having lived far away. The law enjoins that in an application made by co-sharer tenant all other co-sharer tenants of the holding shall be made parties. In this case it has been concurrently found by the courts below that some of the co-sharer tenants by inheritance were not made parties. Now the question is whether for the omission in making the left out co-sharer tenants parties in the case, the case shall fill on that account or not. In other words whether the making of all the co-sharer tenants by inheritance parties in the case is mandatory or directory. 

 12. Mr. Mokhtar Hossain referred to the decision in the case of Abdus Samad Vs. Sohrab Ali reported in 33 DLR Appellate Division, page 113 which was a later decision of the Appealable In this decision the earlier decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Matilal Sikdar Vs. Benodini Dashi was considered and according to this decision impleading of persons who are necessary parties to a pre-emption application is mandatory according to sub section 2 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and it is not controlled by Order I Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It has also been held in this decision that plea of non-joinder of necessary parties should be taken before the trial and if the party seeking pre-emption fails to implead such a party whose existence is disclosed the right of pre-emption is lost. It has also been held that a co-sharer in the holding cannot be allowed to purchase the entire land without impleading the other co-sharers and thereby depriving them from getting share. 

 13. It may also be noted that according to sub section 4 of section 96 of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act upon an application for pre-emption by one co-sharer, other co-sharers having notice of the application have a legal right to apply to join in the same application and to have rate able pre-emption. So this provision of law will be frustrated if some co-sharers are not made parties in the pre-emption case. From this also it must be held that making of all the co-sharers parties in the case for pre-emption is mandatory.
